title: Option to change graph color when it reaches a high level
line: System Monitor widgets can now turn a sensor orange or red when its value goes above a warning or critical percentage you choose.
explanation: System Monitor faces always drew each sensor in its fixed color, whatever its value, so a nearly full memory pie or a maxed-out CPU core looked exactly like an idle one. There was no setting anywhere to react to high values. The change adds two settings to the shared Appearance page, "Use Warning Color Above" and "Use Critical Color Above" (percent of the sensor's own range, "Never" by default), and the shared face code then swaps a sensor's color for the theme's warning (orange) or critical (red) color while its value is at or above the threshold, in every display style.

commits.message:
faces: add an option to show sensors in warning colors above a threshold

System Monitor widgets always draw a sensor in its own color, so there is
no way to notice at a glance that memory or a CPU core is nearly full. Add
warning and critical thresholds to the appearance settings, off by default.

BUG: 495130

media.caption: Before: memory and CPU core widgets always use their fixed sensor colors, however high the values
After: memory above its critical threshold is red; CPU cores above 5% are orange and above 10% red, idle cores keep their own color
Before: the Appearance settings have no threshold option
After: new Use Warning/Critical Color Above settings; applying 35% turns the memory pie red right away
